header.name: Quantum Optics
header.description: The quantum optical description of light-matter interaction is essential for quantum communication, post-quatum cryptography, quantum computing and quantum circuits. These state-of-the art technologies require manipulation of quantum states through time-dependent interactions. The goal of this course is to equip the students with a solid understanding of the non-classical states of light and the models used to describe the much needed interaction for manipulation of quantum systems. The applications of the concepts developed are thoroughly explored towards the end of the course.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are be able to describe electromagnetic fields in the quantum mechanical framework and explain the concept of photon.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to determine photon statistics of coherent states and summarize its applications.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to distinguish between strong and week coupling regime and describe time-dependent interaction between light and two state systems.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to apply Jaynes-Cummings model to practical systems and construct all-optical logic gates.

lecture_topics: Electrodynamics in reciprocal space and normal variables

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Project topics to be assigned towards the end of 6th week

lecture_topics: Light-matter interaction: Dipole Hamiltonian, Rabi Splitting
Applications: Quantum dots in optical cavities: Anharmonic dressed ladder
Quantum wells in in optical cavities: exciton polaritons
